title: A Kingdom Split, a King Regroups
overview: After the northern tribes break away, King Rehoboam calls off a civil war, strengthens his smaller kingdom of Judah, and gains support from people who move south to keep worshiping at Jerusalem.

parts.label: A civil war called off (vv. 1-4)
parts.note: Rehoboam gathers an army to win back the northern tribes, who had just rejected him and made Jeroboam their king. A prophet named Shemaiah brings word from the LORD not to fight their own relatives because this split is God's doing, and they go home.

parts.label: Fortress towns built (vv. 5-12)
parts.note: Since he cannot reunite the kingdom, Rehoboam protects what he has by fortifying fifteen towns and stocking them with commanders, food, oil, wine, shields and spears. Many of these towns face south and west, so many scholars think he feared Egypt as well as the north, and Egypt does invade in the next chapter.

parts.label: Priests and worshipers move south (vv. 13-17)
parts.note: Jeroboam set up his own shrines with calf statues and what may be goat images (the exact meaning of that word is debated), and he appointed his own priests. So the Levites, the tribe set apart to serve at worship, left their land, and northerners devoted to the LORD followed them to Jerusalem, which strengthened Judah for three years.

parts.label: Rehoboam's wives and children (vv. 18-21)
parts.note: His two named wives both came from David's extended family, though the text does not say why he chose them. Maakah is called Absalom's daughter but may have been his granddaughter, and Rehoboam loved her most among 18 wives and 60 concubines, who were secondary wives of lower status.

parts.label: Choosing an heir (vv. 22-23)
parts.note: Rehoboam named Maakah's son Abijah as the next king, apparently passing over older sons, and placed his other sons in the fortress towns with supplies and wives. The text calls this wise without saying why, and a common reading is that it gave them real roles while keeping them apart so they would not compete for the throne.

think: The Levites left their land and homes rather than take part in worship they could not accept. Is there anything you would hold on to even if it cost you that much?
